name: Pseudo-3D flight ground
oneLiner: Call a mount on the top-down map and the ground zooms, turns and tilts into a perspective, scanline-scaled plane with a horizon sky band; fly (turn with a slight horizon tilt, speed up, slow down) over the wrapping world past distance-scaled billboards, with the mount's shadow below and a mini-map, then land only on flat ground and the view eases back to the walking map.
fits: top-down RPG overworld (airship, bird, dragon, glider travel)
top-down adventure with a mount or vehicle
exploration games with islands or large maps
notFor: racing on a track (needs track physics, laps and opponents, a different element)
true 3D terrain with height (the ground is one flat plane; heights are billboards)
isometric maps (the texture is a north-up grid)

needs: a top-down tile map: size, tile size, tile id per tile, the tile art (canvas per tile) or a colour per tile id
a landing rule per tile: canLand(tx, ty) (flat, walkable, free)
the walking camera {x, y} (world px at the view's top-left) and the map viewport rect in the canvas
the hero's world position and facing at take-off, and a way to place the hero (and recompute the camera) at the landing tile
a fixed-step update (60 Hz) and the map draw pass, where the flight view replaces the walking map while busy
input: a free take-off key; arrows/WASD and a land key are routed to the module while flying
optional: billboard list (trees, rocks, houses, towns), mini-map markers (goals)
provides: busy flag (take-off, flight, landing): the walking update is skipped meanwhile
event onLand {tx, ty, x, y} at the start of a landing, onLanded at its end, onLandDenied {tx, ty}, onPhase(rising|flying|landing|walk)
data mount anchor {x, top, w, h, footY} and sprite rect in canvas px, for effects and numbers
data project(wx, wy, wz) -> screen point, for anything the game draws in the flight view
data UI rects of the mini-map, landing prompt and speed gauge
data flight state: phase, progress, x, y, heading, speed, roll, altitude, tile, draw timing

assets: none: ground texture from the host's own tile art; sky, billboards (mountain, peak, tree, pine, town, tower, rock, cloud), mount (bird, glider), mini-map and UI are drawn by code in the module
